title: Willow Care - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Willow Care onboarding to Redwood. Reviewed success criteria, security/compliance needs (SSO, SOC2, KMS), infra options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), pilot scope for chart summarization feature, and next steps including security docs, SSO implementation plan, and pilot bench test scheduling.

Priya - Send proposed pilot config (recommended model, batching, expected QPS) and benchmark template by 2027-07-23
Maya - Setup weekly 30-min sync recurring starting 2027-07-27
Alicia - Provide sample de-identified dataset and success prompts by 2027-07-26

next_steps: Redwood to send SSO/SAML integration guide and SOC2 summary

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-07-20 14:00 PT
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Alicia Gomez (Willow Care - Head of ML), Ben Park (Willow Care - Eng Manager), Sarah Lee (Product Lead), Tom Rivers (IT Security)

Summary (auto): Kickoff call for onboarding. Covered goals/success metrics, security requirements, infra options, pilot scope. Action items and owners noted.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Hayes, AE on the account, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Maya our CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alicia: Hi Jordan, doing well, thanks. Excited to get started.
[00:09] Ben: Thanks, yeah we've been looking forward to this.
[00:11] Maya: Quick note, I'll be handling cadence and onboarding enablement.
[00:15] Jordan: Great. Agenda for today - quick intros, goals and success criteria from Willow, security and networking, recommended pilot scope, and next steps. Any additions?
[00:23] Sarah: That's fine. We'll also want to cover timeline — we have a product launch in Q4 so timeline is a bit compressed.
[00:28] Jordan: Noted. Alicia, can you kick off with your top success criteria?
[00:32] Alicia: Sure. For us, primary metric is accuracy of chart summarization - we want 90% acceptable summaries in clinical review by clinicians. Latency target is sub 800ms p50 for API calls in the UI path, and cost per summary is also a factor - we have to hit our internal budget. We also have strict data residency and audit requirements - logs need to be retained for a year and we need SSO/SAML and RBAC integration.
[00:55] Priya: Good, that's clear. A couple clarifying Qs — when you say latency target, is that end-to-end including network? And do you have a preferred region?
[01:03] Alicia: Ideally we'd be in us-west for latency to our users, but some customers are in the EU so we may need a plan for multi-region later. For pilot, focus on us-west.
[01:12] Ben: On infra, we're running in AWS with strict VPC peering rules. We can't allow outbound traffic from certain subnets without approval.
[01:20] Tom: Also we default to customer-managed KMS for any encryption keys that touch PHI. We can discuss what level of de-identification is acceptable.
[01:28] Jordan: Thanks, that's helpful. On data classification — we typically recommend two approaches for early pilots: hosted with strong contract controls + SOC2 and data deletion policies, or Private VPC/Private deployment for the most sensitive workloads. For your pilot, given timing, we usually suggest hosted for speed unless compliance blocks it.
[01:44] Alicia: Right — we're trying to move fast but Tom may flag KMS requirements.
[01:48] Tom: At minimum, we need audit logs and KMS. If Redwood's hosted option can't support customer-managed KMS, we will need private or dedicated.
[01:57] Priya: To be clear — our hosted offering does support envelope encryption, and we can integrate with customer KMS for some configs, but for full customer-managed HSM-backed keys that's in our Private deployment. We can document tradeoffs.
[02:10] Ben: Can you remind us on dedicated vs hosted — performance and cost differences?
[02:14] Priya: Sure. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and lower variance on latency; it's more expensive in committed monthly cost but lower per-token in heavy sustained throughput. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and faster to get started but you can see more variability and rate limits. For your pilot (small QPS), hosted is usually fine; if you scale to thousands of requests per minute then Dedicated or Private viewport makes sense. Also we have quantization and batching options to reduce cost.
[02:43] Sarah: For the initial pilot, we're looking at user-facing chart summaries in the product flow so latency matters. Is there a recommended model size to hit 800ms p50?
[02:52] Priya: If we target a 1–2k token context and use our optimized 7B-class model with continuous batching and KV cache, you can often hit sub 800ms p50 on us-west on our hosted tier for modest QPS. If not, we can tune batching and sequence length. We'll include a benchmark template.
[03:10] Alicia: Sounds good. What's involved in SSO setup — we use Okta and have SAML 2.0.
[03:14] Maya: We have a standard SAML guide. Jordan will share it. We also support SCIM for user provisioning; that's optional but helpful for RBAC.
[03:22] Jordan: I'll share the SSO/SAML guide and an SOC2 summary doc after the call.
[03:27] Tom: Do you support audit log exports into our SIEM?
[03:30] Priya: Yes — logs can be exported to S3 or streamed to a customer's SIEM via our logging integration. For Private deployments we have more comprehensive in-cluster audit capability.
[03:41] Ben: On networking, we need to know which ports and cidr blocks to open for peering.
[03:46] Priya: We'll send a network requirements doc; typically for hosted it's outbound TLS to our API endpoints and for VPC peering we provide the VPC ranges. We'll capture that as an action item.
[03:57] Alicia: For data, we'll provide de-identified chart excerpts for the pilot. Any specific format?
[04:03] Priya: JSONL with one example per line is easiest. We'll include a template in the benchmark doc.
[04:08] Jordan: Great. Let's walk through a proposed pilot flow — 2-week bench test then 4-week pilot in prod-ish environment. Bench test: you give sample data, we run a 48h performance and quality run with metrics and a result spreadsheet. Pilot: integrate API into UI behind feature flag, shadow traffic then ramp. Does that timeline map to your Q4 launch?
[04:28] Sarah: Yes, if bench test is early August and pilot in mid-August to September, we can be ready to evaluate for Q4.
[04:35] Alicia: We also need to involve clinical reviewers for qualitative scoring. We'll arrange that.
[04:40] Priya: For scoring we'll provide an evaluation harness that supports human labels and automatic metrics; you can set pass/fail thresholds.
[04:47] Tom: About compliance paperwork — can you send your data processing addendum and indicate data residency guarantees?
[04:53] Jordan: Yes, we'll send DPA and our standard data residency commitments. For enterprise we can sign amendments.
[04:59] Ben: Any blockers on our side we should consider? We need approval for peering and for outbound traffic, that can take 3–5 business days.
[05:06] Maya: We'll factor that into the timeline; Tom, Ben, please share the network approver contact.
[05:11] Tom: Will do.
[05:13] [05:13] Customer question about model explainability
[05:15] Alicia: For clinician-facing summaries we need traceability — can Redwood provide token-level tracing or provenance?
[05:20] Priya: We have tracing hooks and can surface confidence metadata; full token-level logs are available in Private or Dedicated. Hosted can provide request/response logs and confidence scores but not full internal attention maps. We'll document options.
[05:35] Jordan: OK let's capture action items and next steps. Maya, can you run through the owners?
[05:40] Maya: Sure. Jordan will send onboarding checklist, SSO guide, SOC2 summary and DPA. Priya will send pilot config and benchmark template. We'll schedule weekly 30-min sync starting 2027-07-27. Customer to provide sample de-identified dataset, network contacts, and confirm KMS preferences.
[05:57] Alicia: Quick Q — about KMS, if we need customer-managed keys, what's the lead time for a Private deployment?
[06:04] Priya: Private deployments typically take 4–8 weeks for provisioning depending on network approvals. We can discuss interim mitigations for the pilot.
[06:12] Ben: Ok that's good to know.
[06:15] Jordan: Any other concerns?
[06:17] Sarah: One small ask — can you include a short runbook for failure modes in the pilot (fallback policies)?
[06:23] Priya: Yes, we'll include fallback to a smaller model, retry/backoff guidance, and canary rollout notes.
[06:29] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[06:33] Alicia: Thanks all. Looking forward to it.

Recap and explicit next steps (auto):
- Jordan to send onboarding checklist + SSO/SAML guide, SOC2 summary, DPA (due 2027-07-22).
- Priya to send pilot config, model recommendation, benchmark template (due 2027-07-23).
- Maya to create weekly sync invite (start 2027-07-27).
- Customer: provide de-identified dataset and network approver contacts (due 2027-07-26 / 2027-07-24).

References shared: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding-checklist (link), pilot-benchmark-template.xlsx (link), security/soc2-summary.pdf (link).

End of transcript.
